The response contains ranked interpretations, each with an optional domain_hint and context_clues, plus is_ambiguous. Present these alternatives to a caller or reviewer when context is insufficient to choose one interpretation safely. max_interpretations defaults to 5 and is clamped to 1–10.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Code Meaning INVALID_INPUT Empty or whitespace-only text, returned before the model is called BACKEND_UNAVAIL The LLM endpoint is unavailable, unauthenticated, or not configured QUERY_ERROR The model request failed or its structured response could not be parsed

docs.title: Typical flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR T[Noisy clinical text] --> D[text_decompose or text_disambiguate] D --> N[Optional text_normalize or text_mapping_cleanup] N --> S[Search or concept_candidate_bundle] S --> G[concept_ground or human review]

The LLM output is an input to retrieval, not a mapping decision. Keep the model's confidence and notes available if a later reviewer needs to understand how the search phrase was produced.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Groundworkers uses the shared OMOP stack configuration managed by oa-configurator. The file holds database connections, models, and other shared resources. The [tools.groundworkers] section selects which entries Groundworkers uses and sets its own defaults.

For a guided setup, start with Initial local setup. This page explains the file layout and individual settings.

docs.title: Runtime entrypoints
docs.text:
Open the setup console to create or edit a configuration:

groundworkers tui

Install the console with pip install "groundworkers[tui]". The console edits configuration and runs checks; it does not start an MCP or REST service.

docs.title: Choose the configuration file
docs.text:
The CLI selects a file in this order:

  1. --config-path /path/to/config.toml.
  2. OA_CONFIG_PATH supplied by your shell or client environment.
  3. OA_CONFIG_PATH saved in ~/.config/omop/groundworkers.env.
  4. The default, ~/.config/omop/config.toml.

The console can remember a selected location in groundworkers.env; that file records the location of the TOML file, not a second set of runtime settings. An unusable environment path is reported so you can correct it. Use an explicit path when you need to be sure which configuration is selected:

groundworkers tui --config-path /path/to/config.toml
groundworkers --config-path /path/to/config.toml --describe

For a configuration managed by a deployment or copied from elsewhere, use:

groundworkers tui --config-path /path/to/config.toml --config-read-only

This disables configuration edits in the console. Database preparation and embedding population are separate operations that can still write to their target stores. Edit the authoritative configuration source, then reopen the console to check it. Restart a running service after changing its configuration.

docs.title: Configuration ownership
docs.text:
Shared resources have their own entries so several packages can use the same connection or model:

Concern Where it lives Physical connection credentials and endpoints [connections.*] Logical databases, schemas, and CDM/vocabulary roles [databases.*] Model provider endpoints and credentials [providers.*] Model identity and capabilities [models.*] Vector-store backend and its database [vector_stores.*] Which of those entries Groundworkers uses, plus MCP/REST defaults, grounding policy, source-planning, knowledge-pack, and semantic-projection settings [tools.groundworkers]

Groundworkers references these entries by name and resolves them through oa-configurator. Its core runtime reads [tools.groundworkers] and the shared entries it names. Maintenance commands and installed plugins use their own package sections, as described below.

docs.title: Typical TOML shape
docs.text:
This example includes a CDM connection, PostgreSQL embeddings, and an Ollama chat model. Replace the connection details and choose models available from your provider. The model names and grounding threshold are examples, not required defaults.

[connections.cdm_main]
dialect = "postgresql+psycopg"
host = "localhost"
port = 5432
user = "omop"
password = "replace-me"
database_name = "omop"

[databases.cdm_db]
kind = "cdm"
connection = "cdm_main"
cdm_schema = "public"
vocab_schema = "public"

[providers.local_ollama]
provider = "ollama"
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"

[models.embedding_model]
provider = "local_ollama"
model = "qwen3-embedding:0.6b"
embedding_dim = 1024
embeddings = true

[models.chat_model]
provider = "local_ollama"
model = "qwen3:8b"
structured_output = true

[vector_stores.embeddings]
backend_type = "pgvector"
database = "vector_db"

[databases.vector_db]
kind = "generic"
connection = "cdm_main"
schema_name = "groundworkers"

[tools.groundworkers]
cdm_db = "cdm_db"
embedding_model_name = "embedding_model"
llm_model_name = "chat_model"
vector_store_name = "embeddings"
app_name = "groundworkers"

mcp_transport = "streamable-http"
mcp_host = "127.0.0.1"
mcp_port = 8000

rest_host = "127.0.0.1"
rest_port = 8080
rest_base_path = "/v1"

grounding_min_fulltext_overlap = 0.5
grounding_max_depth = 5

source_planning_llm_assisted_enabled = true

[tools.omop_emb]
cdm_db = "cdm_db"
embedding_model_name = "embedding_model"
vector_store_name = "embeddings"

[tools.omop_alchemy]
cdm_db = "cdm_db"

[tools.omop_graph]
cdm_db = "cdm_db"

Settings are flat, grouped by name prefix. For example, omop-config configure groundworkers --grounding-max-depth 6 updates that field without changing its neighbours.

For a CDM-only setup, keep the connection, CDM database, and [tools.groundworkers] entries. Omit the model and vector-store references and their unused definitions. Lexical operations remain available, although some searches need prepared indexes. See Runtime combinations.

The setup console also configures the companion commands it uses for maintenance:

Package section Used for [tools.omop_emb] Embedding population, using the same CDM, model, and vector-store references. Written when both embedding references are configured. [tools.omop_alchemy] and [tools.omop_graph] CDM schema, search-index, and graph preparation, using the same cdm_db reference.

These sections point to the shared resources; they do not duplicate connection details or credentials. If you edit the file by hand, keep the references aligned before running maintenance. The core Groundworkers runtime does not take its graph or embedding settings from those companion sections.

docs.title: Reference fields
docs.text:
Field References Required cdm_db a [databases.*] entry with kind = "cdm" yes embedding_model_name a [models.*] entry no llm_model_name a [models.*] entry no vector_store_name a [vector_stores.*] entry no

cdm_db defaults to the name cdm_db, which must resolve to a CDM database entry. The other references are optional.

embedding_model_name selects the model for concept embeddings and live query encoding; llm_model_name selects the chat model. They can use different providers, and either can be left unset. They can share a model entry if it supports both capabilities. Chat tools are registered when llm_model_name resolves; use the console checks to verify that the provider and model actually work.

docs.title: A separate vocabulary connection
docs.text:
If the vocabulary tables live in another database, define its connection and set vocab_connection on the CDM database entry:

[connections.vocab_main]
dialect = "postgresql+psycopg"
host = "localhost"
port = 5432
user = "omop"
password = "replace-me"
database_name = "vocabulary"

[databases.cdm_db]
kind = "cdm"
connection = "cdm_main"
cdm_schema = "public"
vocab_connection = "vocab_main"
vocab_schema = "public"

Vocabulary reads use vocab_connection and vocab_schema. If you omit vocab_connection, they use the main CDM connection. Different schemas on the same connection need only separate cdm_schema and vocab_schema values.

docs.title: app_name
docs.text:
Application identity used by:

  • MCP server naming
  • REST application title
  • runtime describe output

Default: groundworkers

docs.title: MCP transport (mcp_*)
docs.text:
Default MCP startup settings used when you do not override them on the CLI.

Field Type Default mcp_transport stdio | sse | streamable-http stdio mcp_host str 127.0.0.1 mcp_port int 8000

docs.title: REST transport (rest_*)
docs.text:
REST is selected explicitly with --transport rest; it is not started alongside MCP. These settings provide defaults when that transport is selected.

Field Type Default rest_host str 127.0.0.1 rest_port int 8080 rest_base_path str /v1

rest_base_path is validated to begin with /.

docs.title: llm_model_name and chat
docs.text:
Text preparation, domain classification, and assisted source planning use the model named by llm_model_name. Its provider entry holds the endpoint and credentials:

[providers.local_ollama]
provider = "ollama"
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"
api_key = "…"

[models.chat_model]
provider = "local_ollama"
model = "qwen3:8b"
structured_output = true

[tools.groundworkers]
llm_model_name = "chat_model"

Set structured_output = true only for a model that supports structured responses. Model capabilities are explicit declarations, not tests of the provider. Configure the provider and select the model in Chat Model, then use Chat to check chat completion and structured output.

For an embedding model, declare embeddings = true. Its dimensions and any document_prefix or query_prefix must match the model and stored vectors. The embedding setup flow helps select these settings; Check model tests provider encoding and checks it against the store registration.

docs.title: Grounding (grounding_*)
docs.text:
These settings control Groundworkers' grounding policy. Other graph traversal limits are supplied with individual tool calls.

Field Type Default grounding_min_fulltext_overlap float 0.0 grounding_max_depth int (1-10) 5

grounding_min_fulltext_overlap must be between 0.0 and 1.0. It is the minimum proportion of query tokens that must appear in a matched concept name for a full-text hit to be accepted; below the threshold grounding falls through to the next tier.

grounding_max_depth bounds the hierarchy distance between a grounding candidate and a required parent concept, or the identity-hop count when grounding runs without parent_ids.

docs.title: Concept flag contract
docs.text:
Grounding results carry strict OMOP flags:

Field Meaning standard_concept true only for raw standard_concept = 'S' classification_concept true only for raw standard_concept = 'C' is_active invalid_reason unset, treating blank and whitespace-only as active

Grounding can legitimately land on a classification concept (an ATC or CPT4 hierarchy node). Those are valid hierarchy positions but not valid mapping targets for a CDM entity field, so check the flags rather than assuming every result is standard.

concept_ground also accepts standard_only and active_only for each call; both default to false. They filter the candidates considered during resolution. In this resolver, standard_only admits both S and C candidates, so it does not guarantee that every returned concept has standard_concept = true.

docs.title: Source planning (source_planning_*)
docs.text:
Field Type Default source_planning_llm_assisted_enabled bool true

When enabled and a chat model is configured, assisted source planning can use that model to classify ambiguous columns. Turning this off leaves deterministic source planning available. It does not disable other chat-backed tools.

docs.title: Knowledge packs (knowledge_*)
docs.text:
Field Type Default knowledge_packs_root str \| null null

groundworkers includes bundled baseline knowledge packs as part of the package. Set knowledge_packs_root when you want to add site-specific or localisation packs on top of that baseline.

Point knowledge_packs_root directly to the directory containing the layer directories:

[tools.groundworkers]
knowledge_packs_root = "./my-knowledge/packs"

my-knowledge/
  packs/                 # knowledge_packs_root points here
    localisation/
      nacc-uds-v4/
        manifest.yaml
        guidance.md

Relative paths resolve against the TOML file's directory; ~ is expanded. A configured pack with the same layer and name replaces the bundled copy. Other bundled packs remain available. These knowledge packs are separate from prompt workflows supplied by plugins; see Working with prompts.

docs.title: Semantic projection (semantic_projection_*)
docs.text:
Field Type Default semantic_projection_enabled bool false

Enable this to expose the semantic_project MCP tool. Projection uses a grounded concept and source context to produce CDM rows; it needs no embedding or chat model.

[tools.groundworkers]
semantic_projection_enabled = true

docs.title: What becomes available at runtime
docs.text: Configuration determines which tools are registered. Registration does not establish that a database, model endpoint, or store is ready: check connections, model compatibility, and coverage separately in the console.

docs.title: With cdm_db alone
docs.text: Concept lookup, lexical search and grounding, graph and mapping tools, deterministic source planning, knowledge packs, and system tools are available. Some search and graph operations need prepared indexes or supporting objects. No separate [tools.omop_graph] section is needed by the core runtime.

docs.title: With vector_store_name alone
docs.text:
Stored-vector operations remain available without a live embedding model. For example, embedding_neighbours can find neighbours of a concept already in the store. Supply model_name when needed to select the stored model.

Live text encoding, text-based embedding search, and the graph's embedding grounding tier need embedding_model_name as well.

docs.title: With embedding_model_name and vector_store_name
docs.text:
Both references enable live embedding search and embedding-backed grounding and mapping. The provider must be reachable and compatible vectors must already exist in the store. With a model reference alone, embedding store operations remain unavailable.

Groundworkers opens the store read-only for queries, status, and coverage checks. Store initialization and population are explicit write operations. Searches never populate missing vectors. See Initial local setup for the preparation steps.

The setup wizard uses the groundworkers schema for PostgreSQL vector storage. The model registry and configuration provenance use their packages' reserved schemas. SQLite uses its database file without a schema. Each database supports one store per model: reuse an existing registration or choose a different database for another store of that model.

A LEGACY_REGISTRY error means the store layout is incompatible. Groundworkers does not migrate legacy stores automatically; inspect the diagnostic and use the migration guidance for your installed storage package. Avoid treating a registry error as an empty store.

docs.title: With groundworkers.llm_model_name configured
docs.text: Text preparation and domain classification tools are registered. Assisted source planning is also available when source_planning_llm_assisted_enabled = true. The embedding model is independent of this choice.

docs.title: With semantic_projection_enabled = true
docs.text: The semantic_project MCP tool is registered. Projection is deterministic and uses no model. See Semantic projection for its inputs and results.

docs.title: Plugin configuration
docs.text:
Installed plugins can have their own [tools.<plugin_name>] settings and references to shared resources. They may provide console configuration pages or additional setup steps. Install plugins in the Groundworkers environment, follow their configuration guide, and restart the host after installation or configuration changes.

Use groundworkers --describe to check which plugins and tools were registered. Plugins that provide readiness checks can report missing configuration or dependencies in the console. Plugin settings belong to the plugin; they are not additional fields in [tools.groundworkers].

docs.title: CLI selection rules
docs.text:
MCP uses the configured mcp_* defaults unless you override them on the command line. REST is selected explicitly and uses the rest_* defaults. --host and --port override the bind address for the chosen HTTP transport.

groundworkers --config-path /path/to/config.toml --describe
groundworkers --transport streamable-http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
groundworkers --transport rest --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

Use separate TOML files for separate environments, selected with --config-path or OA_CONFIG_PATH. See Integrations for client examples.

docs.title: Direct Python example
docs.text:
build_app_config() loads the active shared stack. Supply config_path to select a file explicitly, or use build_app_config_from_stack(stack) when your application already has a StackConfig object.

The Python helpers do not load groundworkers.env; pass config_path explicitly if you rely on a location remembered by the console.

from groundworkers.app import build_application
from groundworkers.bootstrap import build_app_config

config = build_app_config(config_path="/path/to/config.toml")
app = build_application(config)

grounding = app.services.grounding
mapping = app.services.mapping

Build the application once and reuse it. Optional services such as app.services.text are None when they are not configured. A service object being present does not prove its external dependencies are reachable.

config.describe() returns a redacted summary keyed by database, model, llm_model, vector_store, stack, groundworkers, and app_name. CDM schema keys are cdm_schema and vocab_schema; generic/vector-store databases continue to use schema_name. Passwords and API keys are masked; safe URLs never carry credentials.

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
pip install groundworkers
# or
uv pip install groundworkers

This installs both the Python library and the groundworkers CLI.

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text:
Use extras to match the capabilities you plan to run:

Extra Enables embedding-pgvector pgvector embedding backend support embedding-faiss FAISS sidecar acceleration for embedding search xlsx XLSX source-planning input support pdf PDF source-planning input support docx DOCX source-planning input support all_source XLSX, PDF, and DOCX source-planning input support dev Test, lint, docs, and local development tooling

Examples:

pip install "groundworkers[tui,embedding-pgvector]"
pip install "groundworkers[all_source]"

docs.title: Shared stack prerequisite
docs.text:
groundworkers runs against the shared OMOP stack config managed by oa-configurator. In a typical setup you configure:

omop-config configure groundworkers

That writes the [tools.groundworkers] section and the [connections.*] and [databases.*] entries it references. Embedding-backed capabilities need two further named entries — a [models.*] embedding model and a [vector_stores.*] store — which the setup console can create for you:

groundworkers --tui

Groundworkers reads only its own package section plus the named entries it references. It does not read [tools.omop_graph] or [tools.omop_emb].

By default the runtime reads ~/.config/omop/config.toml.

You can override that at startup with:

  • OA_CONFIG_PATH
  • groundworkers --config-path ...

Use separate config files for separate environments and select one with --config-path or OA_CONFIG_PATH.

docs.title: Run as an MCP service
docs.text:
Use stdio when the caller is spawning groundworkers directly:

groundworkers

Use streamable-http for a shared remote service:

groundworkers \
  --transport streamable-http \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000

Inspect the active runtime and registered MCP surface without starting the service:

groundworkers --describe

docs.title: Run as a REST service
docs.text:
groundworkers also exposes a curated REST transport over the same service layer:

groundworkers \
  --transport rest \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080

The REST routes are:

  • POST /v1/mapping/candidate-bundle
  • POST /v1/source-planning/assisted-plan
  • GET /healthz

docs.title: Use as a direct Python library
docs.text:
from groundworkers.app import build_application
from groundworkers.bootstrap import build_app_config

config = build_app_config()
app = build_application(config)

mapping = app.services.mapping

Build the application once at startup and reuse it. The same runtime object works for direct Python calls, MCP registration, and REST startup.

docs.title: Development install
docs.text:
From the repository root:

uv sync --extra dev

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Groundworkers exposes the same configured capability layer through MCP, REST, and direct Python. Choose the interface for the caller, not for a different implementation:

Caller or requirement Interface Agent needs discoverable tools, prompts, and resources MCP Application needs a small, stable HTTP workflow contract REST Python process owns batching, evaluation, or orchestration Direct Python

See Concepts and capability choices for what the capabilities mean. This page shows how to start each interface.

docs.title: Start the server
docs.text:
Use stdio when the MCP client starts the process itself:

groundworkers

Use Streamable HTTP for a shared service:

groundworkers \
  --transport streamable-http \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000

The older sse transport is also accepted. --describe loads the selected configuration, builds the runtime, and prints the active tools, prompts, resources, and redacted configuration without starting a server:

groundworkers --describe

The available tool surface depends on configuration. For example, embedding tools need an embedding store, text and domain tools need a chat model, knowledge tools need a packs root, and semantic projection is explicitly opt-in.

docs.title: Call a tool
docs.text:
The exact client code depends on the MCP SDK. A representative structured call is:

bundle = mcp_client.call_tool(
    "concept_candidate_bundle",
    {"query": "type 2 diabetes", "domain": "Condition"},
)

The response contains retrieval channels, a deduplicated candidate_union, optional standard mappings or context, and warnings. Use groundworkers --describe or MCP discovery rather than assuming every optional tool is present.

docs.title: REST
docs.text: REST is deliberately curated. It currently exposes candidate bundles and assisted source planning rather than mirroring the MCP surface.

docs.title: Start the server
docs.text:
groundworkers \
  --transport rest \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8080

The default routes are:

  • GET /healthz
  • POST /v1/mapping/candidate-bundle
  • POST /v1/source-planning/assisted-plan

The /v1 prefix is configurable with rest_base_path. The current REST transport has a placeholder authentication dependency and does not provide authentication itself; place it behind the deployment's authentication and network controls before exposing it beyond a trusted boundary.

docs.title: Candidate bundle
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/mapping/candidate-bundle \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "type 2 diabetes",
    "domain": "Condition"
  }'

The request model validates and bounds its limits. Backend failures are returned as JSON error objects with an HTTP status appropriate to the error category.

docs.title: Assisted source planning
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/source-planning/assisted-plan \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "content": "field_name,field_label\nhba1c,Haemoglobin A1c\n",
    "filename": "dictionary.csv",
    "caller_hint": "data_dictionary"
  }'

Set content_encoding to base64 when sending binary-safe encoded content. Set include_intermediate when the caller needs the source-planning stages for inspection.

docs.title: Direct Python
docs.text:
Resolve configuration and build one application at startup:

from groundworkers.app import build_application
from groundworkers.bootstrap import build_app_config

config = build_app_config(config_path="/path/to/config.toml")
app = build_application(config)

mapping = app.services.mapping
if mapping is None:
    raise RuntimeError("The CDM vocabulary runtime is not configured.")

bundle = mapping.concept_candidate_bundle(
    "type 2 diabetes",
    domain="Condition",
)

Use app.services.vocab for lexical retrieval, app.services.graph for deterministic concept operations, app.services.grounding for tiered free-text grounding, app.services.mapping for review-oriented workflows, app.services.text and app.services.domain for model-assisted preprocessing, and app.services.source_planning for stateless source analysis. Optional services are None when their prerequisites are absent.

Direct services return normal Python values or typed models. They raise GroundworkersError or ValueError; they do not return MCP error dictionaries. The transport boundary is responsible for serialization and error translation.

SemanticProjectionService is constructed directly because it needs no database, embedding store, or model:

from groundworkers.services.semantic_projection import SemanticProjectionService

projector = SemanticProjectionService()

Build the runtime once and reuse it. Adapters own connection pools and lazy backend state; repeatedly constructing applications can create unnecessary resources.

docs.title: Relationship to groundcrew
docs.text: groundcrew normally consumes Groundworkers over MCP. It owns session state, job lifecycle, and orchestration policy; Groundworkers owns reusable, stateless domain capabilities. A Python application can use the worker services directly when it does not need a remote tool boundary.

docs.title: Working with prompts
docs.text:
Tell the agent what you want to achieve, what you already know, and what is still undecided. Choose a prompt workflow that fits the task and ask for more guidance when needed.

Prompt packs contain reusable instructions for an agent. They can help you develop a study question, review source fields, or make a mapping decision. Groundworkers supplies the tools and guidance; your agent or application runs the conversation and keeps track of decisions. If you need to resume later, ask it to save those decisions and the draft.

docs.title: How the parts fit together
docs.text:
Part Question it addresses Example Workflow guidance What needs to happen next? Establish the study question, gather missing parameters, and prepare a draft for review. User questions (elicitation) What does the user mean or want to decide? Ask which comparison you intend and clarify your answer. Domain knowledge What rules and evidence apply here? Apply the relevant OMOP mapping conventions and source-specific context. Tools What can be looked up or checked? Retrieve concept candidates or check a structured document.

You can use these parts together or separately. An agent can clarify a comparison on its own, or ask the same question as part of a study-design workflow.

Once the agent understands your answer, the workflow still needs to check that it meets the task's requirements before continuing.

docs.title: Start with a goal and relevant context
docs.text:
1. Describe the outcome. Say whether you want an explanation, a draft study question, mapping recommendations, or a document for review.
  2. Supply what you already know. Include relevant source information, constraints, and decisions you have made. Identify anything still undecided.
  3. Choose a pack. Use your client's prompt list, or ask the agent to find a pack that fits the task.
  4. Review the result. Check that it reflects your intent, look at the supporting evidence, and note anything still uncertain.

For example:

Help me turn this study goal into a research question. Use the relevant study workflow, reuse the decisions I have already supplied, and ask one focused question at a time when required information is missing. Keep undecided parameters unresolved and show me the draft for review.

The packs you can use depend on your installation and client. Knowledge packs supply guidance such as mapping rules; workflow packs help organise the task. Finding a knowledge pack does not start a workflow. See the knowledge tools for finding and reading knowledge packs. Workflow packs are available through the optional OHDSI Prompt Registry.

docs.title: Keep track of answers and open questions
docs.text:
A useful question says what needs deciding and gives you enough context to answer. The differences between options should be clear. If none fits, you should be able to explain what you mean.

Your client may show clickable options or a numbered question in chat. In either case, the agent should record your response and wait for an answer before doing work that requires it. A default selection, silence, or closing a dialog is not an answer.

Your response What the agent should preserve An answer Your intended choice or explanation, with clarification where needed. “I will decide later” A deferred decision, with dependent work still pending where the answer is required. “I do not want to answer” A declined question; the workflow determines whether it can continue without that information. An unclear response or no answer An open question, with no answer assumed.

Work can often continue while a question is open. An optional preference can wait; a required study parameter may hold up the final result while still allowing a draft.

You can change an earlier answer. Ask the agent to check which decisions and drafts need updating. For example, changing the comparison may affect the research question while leaving unrelated work intact.

docs.title: Ask for more explanation when you need it
docs.text:
The main instructions should contain the rules needed for routine work. Separate references can explain unfamiliar concepts, give more examples, or cover unusual cases.

The agent can start with those instructions and read more about a particular issue when needed. Required rules belong in the main instructions, so optional background can be left unread without missing a requirement.

You can ask:

Explain why this question is needed and show one relevant example. Use the supporting guidance for this issue rather than loading the whole reference collection.

Separate files help only if the client reads them as needed. Everything the agent reads takes up space in its working context, so ask for the explanation relevant to your question.

docs.title: Save results for review and reuse
docs.text:
Use the conversation to agree what the result means. A structured document makes it easier to save, check, and pass to another tool or team. Ask for a readable summary so you can review it without working directly with JSON.

Passing validation means the document meets the structural checks applied to it. You still need to review its clinical or scientific content and decide whether to approve it. Keep missing decisions visible in the draft; the agent should not fill them with assumptions to make the document look complete.

docs.title: Tell the agent how you prefer to work
docs.text:
You can ask for one question at a time, short or detailed explanations, a preferred language, or a summary before the evidence. For batch review, ask the agent to collect open questions in a review document so it need not interrupt for every row.

These preferences do not change the domain rules. Local or source-specific guidance applies to its intended setting. If guidance conflicts, ask the agent to explain the conflict and what evidence would help resolve it.

Your agent or application controls how questions appear, whether answers are saved, and whether required steps are enforced. Prompt instructions alone cannot guarantee that behaviour. Before relying on a result, ask the agent to show which guidance it used, what you decided, and what is still open.

docs.title: Setup console
docs.text:
The setup console is organized by the capability being configured:

  1. Overview — CDM readiness, optional capabilities, and integration output;
  2. Database — physical connections and logical CDM database entries;
  3. Graph — CDM-backed search and graph preparation;
  4. Performance — graph, trigram, and embedding-index readiness;
  5. LLM provider — provider and model entries for language features;
  6. Embeddings — vector-store setup, coverage, and population;
  7. Chat — checks for the selected chat model;
  8. Configuration — redacted stack configuration; and
  9. Runs — progress and history for durable maintenance work.

For a minimal local setup, use Overview → Configure CDM → Test connections. Optional capabilities can be configured later. Configuration changes show the redacted entries that will be written before they are applied.

See Initial local setup for a complete example.

docs.title: Test lanes
docs.text:
Groundworkers uses distinct lanes because an isolated unit run cannot prove the database, optional parser, plugin-entry-point, or built-wheel contracts.

Lane What it proves CI behavior Unit and service Deterministic policy, adapter boundaries, source planning, transport behavior, and controlled provider responses Runs without a live database or model service Optional dependency Real XLSX, DOCX, and PDF parsing plus missing-extra guidance Required format tests must pass in the all-extras CI lane; missing-extra behavior is simulated PostgreSQL integration Seeded graph retrieval, real pgvector storage and reader behavior, model selection, filters, and embedding-tier grounding Required: every required_integration case must be collected and pass Wheel smoke Base and optional-extra installations, package entry-point discovery, CLI startup, and successful MCP/REST planning operations Builds once and runs outside the checkout Optional live provider Real configured model-provider connectivity Opt-in developer smoke only; never substitutes for seeded embedding tests

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
# Hermetic suite, including real optional-format parsers
uv run pytest -q -ra

# Unit tests only
uv run pytest tests/unit/

# Required PostgreSQL cases; provide a seeded test stack first
GROUNDWORKERS_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/stack.toml \
GROUNDWORKERS_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION=1 \
GROUNDWORKERS_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://... \
uv run pytest -m required_integration -q -ra

# Coverage for local review
COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/groundworkers.coverage uv run pytest -q -ra \
  --cov=groundworkers --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing

The required integration gate derives its cases from the required_integration marker, so every marked case is checked for collection and a passing result. Missing configuration, unavailable adapters, and absent seeded rows fail in that lane. The all-extras CI job applies the same execution check to required_format cases, so a missing parser cannot silently turn the format contract into a skip. Without the corresponding GROUNDWORKERS_REQUIRE_* flag, PostgreSQL and optional-format fixtures remain opt-in and skip with a reason.

docs.title: Configuration and optional provider smoke
docs.text:
Set GROUNDWORKERS_CONFIG_PATH (or GROUNDWORKERS_CONFIG) to the explicit Groundworkers stack file for integration tests. OA_CONFIG_PATH selects the oa-configurator default stack, but does not by itself opt the graph integration tests into a required run. PostgreSQL CI sets both paths and seeds a compact fixture before pytest starts.

The external-provider smoke tests are separate from seeded deterministic embedding tests. To run them locally, set GROUNDWORKERS_RUN_EMBEDDING_INTEGRATION=1, GROUNDWORKERS_CONFIG_PATH, and GROUNDWORKERS_TEST_CONCEPT_ID; they require a configured provider and a concept with stored vectors.

docs.title: Coverage and skip evidence
docs.text: CI publishes coverage.xml and pytest.xml from the hermetic all-extras run. The JUnit report carries named skip reasons. PostgreSQL CI separately enforces the required test list, so optional local skips cannot satisfy that gate. Coverage percentages are review evidence, not a global pass threshold. Prioritize unexecuted behavior at database, provider, transport, and packaging boundaries.

docs.title: Upgrading from Groundworkers 0.6
docs.text: Groundworkers 0.7 uses the oa-configurator 2.0 stack and supports a vocabulary database separate from the primary CDM database.

docs.title: Configuration changes
docs.text:
• Rename the former database schema_name setting to cdm_schema for a CDM database. Use vocab_schema when vocabulary has a distinct schema. Generic databases, including vector-store databases, still use schema_name.
  • SQLite has no schemas. Remove schema settings from SQLite database entries; setup ignores those fields and tells you when they are unavailable.
  • A PostgreSQL vector store colocated with the CDM uses the dedicated groundworkers schema. Its database is a generic entry on the CDM connection:
[databases.groundworkers_vectors]
kind = "generic"
connection = "cdm_main"
schema_name = "groundworkers"
  • Add databases with the 2.0 CLI syntax, for example:
omop-config databases add cdm clinical --connection cdm_main --cdm-schema public
omop-config databases add generic vectors --connection cdm_main --schema-name groundworkers
  • Startup now fails fast if either the primary or vocabulary endpoint cannot be reached. The console prints the first scrubbed cause and a database recovery hint.
  • A pre-3.0 embedding store reports LEGACY_REGISTRY. The migration script is tracked in oa-configurator issue #40; once it ships, Groundworkers will provide the omop-emb migration command.
  • To split the vocabulary, set vocab_connection on the CDM database entry. Groundworkers 0.7 routes vocabulary reads to that connection, including setup diagnostics and graph searches.

docs.title: Plugin changes
docs.text: See Upgrading plugins to Groundworkers 0.7 for the full API checklist. Plugins should require groundworkers>=0.7,<0.8, pass cdm_session_factory for OMOP graph/vocabulary access, and treat embedding_backend_factory() as a read-only EmbeddingStoreReader.
